title: Halo, blue, Spitz & recurrent naevi
summary: Special naevi that worry patients and clinicians: halo naevi with a white ring, blue naevi, Spitz and Reed naevi in children, and moles that regrow in a scar.

glance.think: A mole with a white ring, a steel-blue papule, a fast-growing pink dome in a child, or pigment returning in a scar.
glance.engine: Immune clearance (halo), deep dermal melanocytes (blue), epithelioid/spindle melanocytes (Spitz/Reed), residual cells (recurrent).
glance.backbone: Reassure typical halo and blue naevi; refer Spitz-like lesions in adults, atypical or changing ones; send previous histology with recurrent naevi.
glance.never_miss: Melanoma with regression or a halo; spitzoid melanoma in adults; recurrent melanoma in a scar.

head: Naevus
Key features
Management (IP)
Photo
rows: A naevus with a symmetrical white ring (immune destruction), in children and teens; may be multiple; **association with vitiligo**
Reassure if the central naevus is benign and symmetrical. **Refer an adult (>40) with a new halo or an atypical central lesion** (melanoma can provoke halos). Sun-protect the white ring
Steel-blue, firm, dome-shaped; dermal melanocytes; head, hands, buttocks
Reassure if long-standing and stable. Refer if new in an adult, enlarging, or >1 cm (cellular blue naevus; melanoma DDx; also metastatic melanoma looks blue)
Pink-red or pigmented, dome-shaped, rapidly growing in a **child**; dermoscopy starburst/dotted vessels
Children <12 with a typical lesion: specialist may monitor. **Adolescents/adults: excision** (atypical Spitz tumour and spitzoid melanoma DDx)
Black, symmetrical starburst on the thigh in young women
Pigment returning in a scar after a shave or incomplete excision
Refer **with the previous histology**. It mimics melanoma on dermoscopy

red_flags: A Spitz-like lesion in an adult, an atypical halo naevus, or a recurrent pigmented lesion in a scar: refer on a **suspected cancer pathway**.
